s: BYU’s collection of art started long before the museum was opened. The collection began in 1909 when a painting of a sycamore tree by Utah painter John Hafen was donated. In 1937, Herald R. Clark purchased 85 prints from artist Maynard Dixon. In 1960, the school received artist Mahonri Young’s art collection which included over 10,000 works.
MOA staff has continued to expand the collection by acquiring compelling artworks, primarily focused on American and European art, that will edify and enlighten our community.
